10712122_246bd5c1.text: In the dentate gyrus cells migrate only a few micrometers, from the subgranular zone to the granule cell layer. Cells develop from a precursor cell type in which mitotic events are found

10712122_eeb498fb.text: In mammals the SVZ contains three cell populations important for stem cell proliferation. The proper stem cell population is maintained through slowly dividing astrocyte-like neural stem cells known as type B cells. These cells give rise to actively proliferating type C cells, which in turn give rise to immature neuroblasts, called type A cells. These neuroblasts, not yet neuronally committed, migrate to the olfactory bulb via chain migration by cell-cell contacts.
